speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, last talk to bring us home.

speaker: Unknown
en: We have Arjun and Ronak, co-founders of Trajectory.
zh: 我们有 Arjun 和 Ronak,Trajectory 的联合创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're doing a bunch of interesting research around what I think is one of the hotter topics, continual learning.
zh: 他们正在围绕我认为是最热门的话题之一——持续学习——做一系列有趣的研究。

speaker: Unknown
en: Please welcome Arjun to the stage.
zh: 请欢迎 Arjun 登上舞台。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cool.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's up?
zh: 大家好？

speaker: Unknown
en: How's it going, everyone?
zh: 大家近况如何？

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you so much.
zh: 非常感谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm really excited.
zh: 我真的很兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know I'm close to the last one, so hopefully there's like remaining attention span.
zh: 我知道我接近最后一场了，所以希望大家还剩下一些注意力。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm here.
zh: 我在这儿。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ronak is also back there, so we're together.
zh: Ronak 也在后面，所以我们是在一起的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But let's get started.
zh: 那我们开始吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're trajectory, and we're building the platform for continual learning.
zh: 我们是 Trajectory,我们正在构建持续学习的平台。

speaker: Unknown
en: Who are we?
zh: 我们是谁？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we're working on a really, really cool mission, and that's the most fun part.
zh: 我觉得我们正在做一件非常、非常酷的使命，这是最有趣的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second most fun part is I get to do this with my two best friends, Renek over here, who worked at Windsurf and trains V1 before this, and Michael, who worked on really cool robotic stuff at DeepMind.
zh: 第二有趣的部分是，我可以和我最好的两个朋友一起做这件事，Renek 在这里，他之前在 Windsurf 和 trains V1 工作过，还有 Michael,他在 DeepMind 做过非常酷的机器人方面的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what I wanted to start off with was the worldview that we have and how that shapes
zh: 我想以我们拥有的世界观作为开场，以及它如何塑造

speaker: Unknown
en: Why we think this problem is important.
zh: 我们为什么认为这个问题重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the worldview that we have is that, and it's not a hot take, we are living in an incredible time in human history here.
zh: 我们的世界观是，这不是什么惊人之语，我们正生活在人类历史上一个不可思议的时代。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every single week, it seems like another model is coming out that is leapfrogging the last one.
zh: 看起来每一个星期，都有另一个模型问世，超越上一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's undeniable that models are getting better and better.
zh: 模型正变得越来越好，这一点无可否认。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we think that they're getting better on one axis, and that is IQ.
zh: 但我们认为它们是在一个轴上变得更好，那就是智商。

speaker: Unknown
en: These models are smarter and smarter, but always feels like when you're talking to them, it's their first thing on the job.
zh: 这些模型越来越聪明，但当你和它们交谈时，总感觉像是它们上班的第一天。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you take this analogy of a Terrence Tao in your pocket, that's great, but Terrence Tao day one at an accounting firm,
zh: 所以如果你用「口袋里的 Terrence Tao」这个类比，那很棒，但 Terrence Tao 在一家会计公司上班的第一天，

speaker: Unknown
en: It's probably not the best accountant there, but give him a few years, or honestly maybe even like a few days, he'd probably be really good.
zh: 他可能不是那里最好的会计，但给他几年时间，或者说实话也许只要几天，他可能会变得非常出色。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we have this orthogonal axis of experience that is much more important than we think in conjunction with IQ.
zh: 所以我们有这个与智商正交的经验轴，它的重要性远超我们的想象。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's what we're calling the experience gap, and that is what we want to close as a company.
zh: 我们把它称为经验差距，而这就是我们作为一家公司想要弥合的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, but the question is like how do you
zh: 那么，但问题是，你要如何

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you close that?
zh: 你要如何弥合它？

speaker: Unknown
en: Where does experience come from?
zh: 经验从哪里来？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, it's already out there right now.
zh: 嗯，它现在就已经存在了。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's so many, 100 trillion is a number, but so many tokens out there that are being generated by these agents.
zh: 有非常多——100 万亿是一个数字——有如此多的 token 正由这些智能体生成。

speaker: Unknown
en: You view them or sometimes you don't even view them and they get thrown away.
zh: 你会查看它们，或者有时你甚至不查看它们，它们就被丢弃了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But this is all real work that they're doing.
zh: 但这些都是它们正在做的真实工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then people are acting upon them and then it's being thrown away.
zh: 然后人们对其采取行动，然后它就被丢弃了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so our take as a company, as Gabe mentioned, like our opinionated take, is that this is the signal that we should be learning from.
zh: 所以作为一家公司，正如 Gabe 提到的，我们旗帜鲜明的观点是：这才是我们应该学习的信号。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is also how humans get better.
zh: 这也是人类变好的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in classic AI fashion, like if humans do it, it's probably a good way to mental model off of.
zh: 而且按照经典的人工智能套路，如果人类是这么做的，那它可能就是一个很好的心智模型参照。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so today's agents, they're still slow, expensive, aeroplane over time.
zh: 所以今天的智能体，它们仍然缓慢、昂贵，aeroplane(随时间推移)。

speaker: Unknown
en: You implement them, they probably don't get better.
zh: 你部署了它们，它们可能不会变得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: We want to imagine what learning agents look like, where as they are used by people, they get better and better over time.
zh: 我们想想象一下会学习的智能体是什么样子——随着被人们使用，它们随着时间变得越来越好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And tangibly, this has two good benefits.
zh: 具体来说，这有两个好处。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right away, it gets you much faster, better, cheaper models.
zh: 立竿见影的是，它能让你得到更快、更好、更便宜的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: But more excitingly, it gets you to this goal of systems that compound with use.
zh: 但更令人兴奋的是，它能让你达到这个目标：随着使用而复利增长的系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I want to start off by talking about how we're approaching this problem, and then some interesting stuff for you guys at the end.
zh: 所以我想先谈谈我们是如何着手解决这个问题的，然后在最后给你们一些有趣的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so where it starts off, and this kind of dovetails off of what Harrison was talking about before, is it starts off with traceability.
zh: 一切的起点——这也和之前 Harrison 讲的内容相衔接——是可追溯性。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need to first capture these interactions, capture this experience that's being thrown away.
zh: 我们需要首先捕捉这些交互，捕捉这些正在被丢弃的经验。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's step number one.
zh: 所以这是第一步。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then step number two, and this is where we start getting into our research, the way we view the company we're building is we are building a product to allow for continual learning, but we're doing cutting-edge research under every single one of them to make this possible.
zh: 然后第二步，这是我们开始进入我们研究的地方——我们看待所构建公司的方式是，我们正在构建一个支持持续学习的产品，但在每一个环节之下，我们都在做尖端研究来实现这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so...
zh: 所以……

speaker: Unknown
en: You have all these interactions, and the next thing we're building is this idea of a model spec.
zh: 你有所有这些交互，我们接下来要构建的就是这个「模型规范」的概念。

speaker: Unknown
en: This idea that you need to have a way to define what do I want my agent to do and have the agent learn against that.
zh: 这个想法是，你需要有一种方式来定义我想让我的智能体做什么，并让智能体据此学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're doing really cool research here on how to extract user interactions, turn that into reward, extract traces, and turn that into exact specs of what you want your agent to do.
zh: 所以我们在这里做很酷的研究，关于如何提取用户交互，将其转化为奖励，提取轨迹，并将其转化为你希望智能体做什么的精确规范。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, cool.
zh: 好，不错。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have what you want your agent to do.
zh: 你有了想让智能体做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you do with that?
zh: 那你拿它做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, there's two surfaces.
zh: 嗯，有两个层面。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is the models, right?
zh: 一是模型，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: You want your models to learn from actual interactions here.
zh: 你想让你的模型从真实的交互中学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we're doing really cool research on algorithms like SDPO and things along those lines where we're using RL to take these full long traces and improve models over time.
zh: 所以我们正在做很酷的研究，比如 SDPO 这类算法及类似方向，我们用 RL 来利用这些完整的长轨迹，随时间不断改进模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: But models are not the only thing.
zh: 但模型不是唯一的层面。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have harnesses as well.
zh: 你还有 harness。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're doing a lot of really cool research on
zh: 我们正在做很多很酷的研究，关于

speaker: Unknown
en: When you have good feedback from people, does that go to a harness or does that go to a model?
zh: 当你从用户那里得到好的反馈时，它应该给 harness 还是给模型？

speaker: Unknown
en: An example here is if it's like a fact, like this person, this company has been delisted, right?
zh: 这里的一个例子是，如果它是一个事实，比如这家公司已经退市了，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: You probably don't want to train that knowledge into the model.
zh: 你大概不会想把这类知识训练进模型里。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's probably context that should be available to the harness.
zh: 它大概是应该提供给 harness 的上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that is kind of how we're splitting things, and that is the product that we're building, allowing you to go from real interactions all the way to specs of what you want your agent to get better at to better models and then better harnesses, and then being able to deploy those models right away and then using your product.
zh: 所以这就是我们大致的拆分方式，也就是我们正在构建的产品，让你能够从真实交互出发，一直到你希望智能体在哪些方面变好的规范，到更好的模型，再到更好的 harness，然后能够立即部署这些模型，并用于你的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's the world we want to get to.
zh: 所以这就是我们想抵达的世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you have built agents, which I'm sure most of you guys have, you probably know that there are so many things that go wrong with every single part of these and how every single one of these is an unsolved problem.
zh: 如果你们构建过智能体——我相信在座大多数人都有——你们可能知道，这些东西的每一个部分都会出很多问题，每一个问题都是未解之谜。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the way I wanted to frame the rest of this is I'm going to imagine that I am like straight from Aladdin and I have like four wishes.
zh: 所以我想这样来组织剩下的内容：我要想象自己就像从《阿拉丁》里走出来一样，我有四个愿望。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what are those wishes that I would ask to like make the agent ecosystem
zh: 那么我会许哪些愿望来让智能体生态系统……

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we have agents today, we have this gap, and there's a level where agents should get to, and after that we can really see the exponential effects of continual learning.
zh: 所以我们今天有了智能体，我们存在这个差距，智能体应该达到某个水平，在那之后我们才能真正看到持续学习的指数级效应。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what are those in?
zh: 那些是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll walk through them step by step, but they're the same four categories I talked about.
zh: 我会逐步过一遍，它们就是我之前讲的同样四个类别。

speaker: Unknown
en: What we would like to see on the traceability side.
zh: 我们希望在可追溯性方面看到什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: What we'd like to see on the eval side, what we'd like to see on the harness side, and what we'd like to see on the model side.
zh: 我们希望在 eval 方面看到什么，在 harness 方面看到什么，以及在模型方面看到什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's start with wish number one.
zh: 那我们从愿望一开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: And how can companies get there faster?
zh: 以及公司如何更快地到达那里？

speaker: Unknown
en: Traceability.
zh: 可追溯性。

speaker: Unknown
en: So two sub-wishes here.
zh: 这里有两个子愿望。

speaker: Unknown
en: Number one is around tracing the entire tree of what happens, including sub-agents.
zh: 第一个是关于追踪整个发生的树，包括子智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: What a lot of companies do is they trace the main action that is happening, but they throw away tool calls or sub-agents that are made, and that makes it very hard to learn from the whole thing that you've done.
zh: 很多公司做的是追踪正在发生的主操作，但他们丢弃了工具调用或产生的子智能体，这让你很难从整个已完成的事情中学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's wish number one.
zh: 所以那是愿望一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sub-wish number two is probably the most important here, and that
zh: 子愿望二可能是这里最重要的，那就是——

speaker: Unknown
en: You should build your product around how you can both capture this interaction data, but also elicit the right amount of feedback so that you can then capture it.
zh: 你应该围绕如何既能捕获这些交互数据，又能引出恰到好处的反馈量来构建你的产品，这样你才能把它捕获下来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a really interesting thing here is, I think the level one way of thinking about this is, okay, let's have like a thumbs up, thumbs down, and like, let's capture that.
zh: 这里有一个很有意思的点，我认为第一层级的思考方式是：好，我们来搞个点赞、点踩之类的，把它捕获下来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that sounds amazing in theory, but it's incredibly noisy.
zh: 这在理论上听起来很棒，但实际上噪音极大。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you've used any coding agent, you know you kind of just like accept everything that the agent does.
zh: 如果你用过任何编程智能体，你知道你基本上就是接受智能体做的一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's only like five commits later that you're like, oh crap, like this broke everything, let me go and undo that.
zh: 往往要过了五个提交之后你才说，哦糟了，这把一切都搞坏了，让我去撤销。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's the corrective behavior, the like the edits, the undos and the retries that both need to be
zh: 所以是纠正性行为，比如编辑、撤销和重试，既需要——

speaker: Unknown
en: Like elicited from the user, but also captured.
zh: 既从用户那里引出，也需要被捕获。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's my wish on traceability.
zh: 所以这就是我在可追溯性上的愿望。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second wish is around evals.
zh: 第二个愿望是关于 eval。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the mental model to use here is your, the product that your user uses should be as similar as, as close to what the eval is done in, in ProWise.
zh: 这里要用的心智模型是：你的用户使用的产品，应该与 eval 进行的环境尽可能相似、尽可能接近。

speaker: Unknown
en: should be as close to where the training is done in.
zh: 应该与训练进行的环境尽可能接近。

speaker: Unknown
en: In an ideal world, these are all the same.
zh: 在理想世界里，这些全部是同一个东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no difference between these.
zh: 它们之间没有任何区别。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this means that evals are drawn from traffic, how people are actually using your product, both how they're using it now and the things that they're requesting on the frontier that might not be possible, all super helpful.
zh: 所以这意味着 eval 来自流量，来自人们实际使用你产品的方式，既包括他们现在怎么用，也包括他们在前沿上提出的可能尚不可行的需求，这些都超有用。

speaker: Unknown
en: Second is making every task rolloutable.
zh: 第二是让每个任务都可以回放。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a pretty big infra challenge, but it's this idea that, hey, if a user has done one thing,
zh: 这是一个相当大的基础设施挑战，但它的想法是，嘿，如果用户做过一件事，

speaker: Unknown
en: Can I somehow replay what the user has done?
zh: 我能不能以某种方式回放用户所做的事情？

speaker: Unknown
en: And that is an incredibly helpful boon to moving forward in this agentic era.
zh: 而这对在这个智能体时代向前推进有着难以置信的帮助。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then lastly, this goes with number one, grading through the real harness.
zh: 然后最后，这个和第一条相关，通过真实 harness 来评分。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not making a variation of the harness, but grading the real harnesses that people use in production.
zh: 不是做一个 harness 的变体，而是对人们在生产环境中使用的真实 harness 进行评分。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that is wish number two.
zh: 这就是第二个愿望。

speaker: Unknown
en: Wish number three, getting into the harness, pretty important.
zh: 愿望三，进入 harness，相当重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: Number one is, and I think the mental model to use here is, I think a lot of products have built their harnesses around models that existed a year or a year and a half ago, where the primary function of the harness was to prevent the agent from doing bad things.
zh: 第一是，我认为这里要用到的思维模型是，我认为很多产品的 harness 是围绕一年或一年半以前的模型构建的，那时 harness 的主要功能是防止智能体做坏事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which was really good when agents would randomly break or have misformatted outputs.
zh: 在智能体会随机出错或输出格式错乱的时候，这确实非常有用。

speaker: Unknown
en: But now we're very much in a let the agents cook world.
zh: 但现在我们非常处于一个「让智能体放开干」的世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think I would view building the harness as not enforcing specific flows that need to be done, but more what are the primitives that your product has, whether that's search tools or private information, and then viewing the agent as orchestrating those primitives and then letting it do that.
zh: 所以我认为应该把构建 harness 视为不是强制执行需要完成的特定流程，而是更多地去想你的产品有哪些原语，无论是搜索工具还是私有信息，然后把智能体视为编排这些原语的角色，然后放手让它去做。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's SubWish 1.
zh: 这是子愿望一。

speaker: Unknown
en: SubWish 2, and this is how we're building our product as well, is making the agent interface as close to the user interface as possible.
zh: 子愿望二，这也是我们构建自己产品的方式，就是让智能体接口尽可能接近用户界面。

speaker: Unknown
en: In an ideal world, every single thing that I can do on your UI, your agent can do via a tool call as well.
zh: 在理想世界里，我能在你的 UI 上做的每一件事，你的智能体也能通过一次工具调用做到。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that is a world that makes training and continual learning so, so much easier.
zh: 我认为那样的世界会让训练和持续学习变得非常、非常容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then lastly, this is a small one, making tool responses informative.
zh: 然后最后，这是一个小的点，让工具响应具有信息量。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's easy to be like, okay, I just want to know the state.
zh: 我觉得很容易就这么想，好，我只是想知道状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's say I'm calling a search tool.
zh: 比如说我在调用一个搜索工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to know the state.
zh: 我想知道状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to see if it worked.
zh: 我想看看它是否成功了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if it's writing to a DB or something, it just writes to it.
zh: 而如果它在写一个数据库或什么东西，它就直接写进去。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what we see often is the response from that tool call will be done, finished.
zh: 而我们经常看到的是，那次工具调用的响应会是「完成、结束」。

speaker: Unknown
en: That sounds good in theory, but from an agent's perspective, it's incredibly confusing.
zh: 这在理论上听起来不错，但从智能体的角度来看，这非常令人困惑。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you're trying to train or learn off of that, there's no signal to learn off of.
zh: 而且如果你想据此进行训练或学习，就没有可学习的信号。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have no idea what actually was written.
zh: 你完全不知道实际写入了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have no idea what actually was read.
zh: 你完全不知道实际读取了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's the last sub-wish under the harness, is to make your tool responses really informative.
zh: 所以这就是 harness 下最后一个子愿望，就是让你的工具响应真正具有信息量。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's wish number three.
zh: 这就是第三个愿望。
